findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door drawer cooler under the grill:
1. Gyro meat (60.9F with probe)
2. Two containers of raw hamburger (60.0F and 62.3F with probe
3. Sliced cheese (63.4F with probe)
4. BBQ Pork (56.8F with probe)
The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC investigated the cooler further and discovered that the power switch had been accidentally turned off. The cooler was turned on and reached 41F during today’s visit. Since the items were discarded and the cooler is operational, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: The inspector observed pests present in the kitchen, dish area, and bar spaces. The insects were observed present on glue traps in all three spaces. The PIC informed the inspector that active pest control measures are being taken. Pest control is currently visiting the facility every two weeks. The inspector recommends writing dates on all glue traps for monitoring purposes, sealing all holes and coving to prevent pest movement, and deep cleaning the floors and equipment to starve out pests. The inspector will spot check the facility to confirm pest reduction in the 30 days (2/17/2026 to avoid weekend and holiday). Ensure receipts of pest control visits are kept in the facility for the inspector to view.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door cooler:
1. Cottage cheese
2. Sour cream
3. Coleslaw
4. Tavern cheese
5. Cut lettuce
6. Cut tomato
7. Caesar dressing
8. Ranch dressing
9. Shredded cheese

These items all measured roughly 50-60 degrees with the infrared thermometer. The digital thermometer for the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC called and scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Since the items were discarded, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Due to the failure of the cooler, these items were voluntarily discarded. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper date marking procedure and a handout was provided.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The 2-door standing cooler was observed to measure 50-60F with the infrared probe. The interior of the cooler was not cold to the touch. The PIC was informed and determined that the cooler was not operational. Maintenance on the cooler was scheduled during the inspection. A follow-up will be conducted on 6/20/2025 to ensure the cooler has been repaired. In the meantime, the 2-door standing cooler cannot be used to store TCS foods. The walk-in will be used until the service is completed.

3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored in metal tubs which were contaminated with dust and food debris. Observed single-use condiment cups to be stored with food contact surfaces exposed or without adequate coverings to protect from dust/debris contamination. Observed large sharpies to be in a container with plastic spoons. Advised PIC to keep containers holding single-use utensils clean and to keep single-use food contact surfaces covered or inverted on a clean surface such as the bottom of a container or clean work surface. Containers holding single-use utensils were washed and contaminated utensils were disposed of during inspection.

(C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: There were no chlorine test strips available during the inspection. The facility had pH test strips. Provide chlorine test strips to ensure sanitizer solutions are at proper concentrations. Test strips provided by the inspector. The proper type of test strips were discussed with the manager. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the hood baffles to have an accumulation of grease. Also, the walk in cooler (WIC) fan was dusty. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned more frequently so they are maintained clean. 
 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed the floor under the fryers and flat top grill to be heavily soiled with food, grease, and other debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned frequently so they are maintained clean. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed the kitchen sani bucket to be at a concentration of 0ppm of bleach. Sani buckets must maintain a concentration between 50ppm and 200ppm of bleach. The sani bucket was remade during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: There were no chlorine test strips available during the inspection. The facility had pH test strips. Provide chlorine test strips to ensure sanitizer solutions are at proper concentrations. Test strips provided by the inspector to correct the violation. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the hood baffles to have an accumulation of grease. Also, the walk in cooler (WIC) fan was dusty. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned more frequently so they are maintained clean. 
 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540. Certified manager arrived after I arrived. Schedule and keep certified manager on duty at all times food is prepared and sold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Foods in the drawers of the low boy are between 44°F and 56°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). Facility voluntarily discarded 4 lbs of bbq pork at 51°F , 3 lbs of brisket at 50°F, 2 lbs of gyro meat at 50°F , 13lbs of 5 oz burger portions at 47°F .  Olives and other items in the top drawer were discarded.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Milk and OJ in the bar cooler of the facility are not marked with a use-by date.  Foods were marked. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Ensure that all items are properly date marked.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly at the ice scoop. Observed the ice scoop holder at the bar to have water in the bottom. The scoop and holder were removed and sanitized. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the soda gun at the bar and the inside of the hot holding unit. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) The floor to the right of the fryers behind and under the pipe on the ground are soiled. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation areas. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Store personal drinks in an area where they will not potentially contaminate food or single service items.  Reference 2-401.11. Cups were removed.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P Thirteen portion cups of ranch are observed to be sitting out at room temperature.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed a box of napkins on the floor in the dry storage area. Store single use items properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14  (P) Chili put to cool at 11am is 107°F. Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.  Three half pans of chili between 107 and 114F were discarded in the garbage. No time or temp on the itmes. No cooling temperature logs kept. Use active methods to properly cool chili in the future.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) Hamburger in the low boy is observed to be 54F. Gyro meat is observed to be held at 56F. Impossible burgers observed to be 56F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadaquiately held food was voluintarily discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2). 28 big burgers, 5 reguarl sized burgers, 7 impossible burgers and approximately 3 pounds of gyro meat were discarded. Technician was called to repair the low boy. Do not use this unit for TCS foods until it is repaired.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 4/30 marked on chili on hot holding unit exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling chili is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15. Keep cooling logs and or place temperature date and time on the food so that time in the temperature danger zone can be adequately evaluated. Food was discarded.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are observed to be stored in sanitizer that is not proper strenght. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Sanitizer bucket was remade to have proper chlorine sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at the wait service area. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12  Floors behind pipes in the kitchen are soiled. (under hand sink and next to walk in door) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 153 - A squeeze bottle of garlic parmesan was observed on the storage rack to the left of the grill. Cook stated he just removed the AM time sticker from the rack. The garlic parmesan was out and in-use since this morning. Also, a jar of garlic parmesan sauce (~1/2 full; 29 FL oz jar) was observed on the shelf above the prep cooler. The products had surface temperatures of 78F (squeeze bottle) and 86F (jar). Both products were removed from the kitchen. Jar of sauce was discarded in the trash, and the squeeze bottle was placed at the dish room 3 part sink to go through ware washing.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage, unless a time control policy is in use. If time control is used, then food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Maintain proper labeling for sauces that are used/discarded based on a time control policy. Discard sauces after 4hrs and start with fresh product.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.210 & 250 - Cheese sauce on range top was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 123F and 128F respectively. Cook stated the product is heated in the double boiler, and the hot water underneath typically helps maintain the product at proper temperature throughout the day. Cook was asked what the cheese sauce was heated to this morning, and the internal temperature was not checked to verify the product reached 165F prior to service today. Cook stated once the product is boiling the staff then assume it is hot enough to turn down the burner and hot hold the product. Based on information provided and temperatures observed the cheese sauce was discarded, and the cook started with fresh product. Additional water was added to the double boiler to also help maintain hotter temperature. 

Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165F/above. After proper reheat, maintain hot potentially hazardous foods at 135F/above while on display and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Old food debris was observed stuck around the hex nuts of bi-metallic stem thermometers and around the top edge of the holders used to house thermometers between uses. Thermometers were cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Thermometers were also calibrated.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Properly clean and sanitize stem thermometers up to every 4hrs after continuous use to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. Maintain a bleach water solution (100-200ppm chlorine) and damp wiping cloths for wiping stem thermometers before and after each use.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 130 - A) Plastic container of pretzel salt on the shelf above the prep cooler was observed to be uncovered. The lid used to cover the container was on the shelf behind the container and was soiled with stuck on food debris. A clean lid was used to cover the pretzel salt.

B) 1. Pan of uncovered fish was observed on the floor in the walkin cooler.
2. Pans ranch dressing and other sauce portioned in soufflé cups were observed on a baking sheet on the floor in the walkin cooler.
Proper storage of foods was discussed.
  
Foods shall be protected at all times, stored at least 6 inches off the floor, and in a clean, covered container once removed from the original package.  Properly store and protect food

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
(R) 750.290 - Blue ice scoop holder at the bar was soiled with general buildup in the bottom. Clean the ice scoop holder daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and protect the scoop from potential contamination.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 1120 - Cook was observed preparing to put on a pair of gloves without first washing hands. Employee just touched the handle of the walkin cooler and other general surfaces.
Bartender was observed making salads and wearing gloves, but hands were not washed in the kitchen prior to putting on gloves. Proper handwashing before putting on gloves/between glove changes was discussed.

Another employee was observed wiping hands with a dry wiping cloth. Employee was advised cloth towels must not be used for wiping hands.

Hands must be properly washed any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with clean equipment. Common towels are prohibited, and wiping cloths must not be used for wiping hands for any reason.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A) Sani-bucket in kitchen was observed at 0ppm chlorine. Cook stated it was prepared earlier that morning. Solution was remade to be at proper concentration (200ppm).

B) Sani-buckets at the bar were observed at less than 100ppm chlorine. Bartender stated the solutions were just prepared within the last hour with luke warm water. Buckets were noted with grimy white buildup on the inside. Bartender stated she would clean the buckets and change the solution when she had time.

Maintain bleach solutions at 100-200ppm chlorine. Change solutions every 2-4hrs throughout the day or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths are heavily soiled. Clean buckets between uses to eliminate buildup inside. Grimy buildup may interfere with solution and cause the sanitizer to break down at an accelerated rate.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Plastic knives were observed with handles and food contact surfaces extended up out of the storage container. Store utensils with handles presented up so food contact surfaces will not be touched by servers when retrieving.

B) Bottom inside containers used for storage of single service items (soufflé cups, lids) were soiled with crumbs and debris. Clean storage containers as needed, and maintain them clean.

C) Black cart holding steam well was observed to be soiled with splash and debris on middle and lower shelves. The lower shelf also had a roll of aluminum foil that was no longer in its original packaging and was soiled with splash. Store the aluminum foil so it is protected from splash and other debris, and keep it in the original packaging when possible. Otherwise, provide another food grade cover for storage.

D) Wire shelving by kitchen handsink and garbage can was soiled with grimy buildup. Wrapped and unwrapped single service articles were observed on the shelving. No apparent splash was observed on the soufflé cups on the shelf directly above the bottom shelf, but this is an area where staff have been advised to refrain from storage of items due to the potential for splash from handwashing and trash being discarded. Items were removed from the area.

Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1060 - Dish room 3 part sink faucet has a leak when the lever is turned to allow for free flowing water. Both the hot and cold water were in the off position, and the hot water did not shut off completely. Get the faucet repaired so water can be turned on and off at both the hot and cold water handles.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) hood and filters (grease); 
B) (R) tongs hanging in kitchen (food debris); and
C) spout of coffee machine above grounds basket (buildup).

Clean food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. tongs, cutting boards, knives, can opener, etc.) must be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled with grease, food debris, and/or general buildup:
A) (R) stainless steel freezer - bottom inside
B) (R) 2 drawer cooler beneath grill - 1. bottom inside (food debris & plastic wrap), 2. doors, 3. handles, & 4. gaskets/surfaces around door seals;
C) (R) fryers - 1. wheels, 2. underneath surfaces, & 3. back ledge inside lower compartments;
D) prep cooler - 1. ledge beneath condenser & general surfaces;  and
E) (R) grill - 1. drip pan, 2. sides, & 3. legs/underneath surfaces. 

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Maintain them clean.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was present at the plumbing beneath the kitchen handsink. Employee stated the maintenance guy was aware of the issue and planned to replace the entire sink. A metal pan is being used to catch dripping water until proper repairs are made. **The metal pan needs to be emptied and cleaned as needed and maintained clean**

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - A) (R) Walls around cooking equipment were soiled with grease buildup. Clean the walls around the cooking equipment.

B) General surfaces underneath the bar 3 part sink were soiled - splash buildup on plumbing and underneath surfaces of basins.  Clean the general surfaces under the bar 3 part sink. 

Walls and attached fixtures must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Seasoning shakers and squeeze bottles with powders and liquids were not labeled as to the contents. Label all shakers and squeeze bottles as to the contents of food products inside. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar, pepper, flour, etc not stored in the original packaging, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Container with fish breading was uncovered in office/dry storage room. Cover foods between uses to protect product from potential contamination. B) Condensation from condenser in walkin cooler was dripping down the inner wall and getting on a bag containing a package of suet, the plastic wrap used to cover a pan of chicken, and lids/pans containing soups. All food items were moved away from the area by inspector, and issue was discussed with management. One employ noted he thought a service call had already been made for the condenser in the walkin (see #29). Do not store foods near area where condensation is an issue until the problem has been resolved. Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.290 - (R) Blue ice scoop holder at bar was soiled inside (debris/puddling water). Clean and sanitize the ice scoop holder daily/as needed and maintain it clean. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.510 - Cook was observed washing hands without using proper technique. Manual faucet was being shut off with freshly washed hands prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with cook and management. Hands must be properly washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, before working with food & clean equipment and any time hands may have been contaminated. Proper technique requires the use of a paper towel or some other barrier to shut off manual faucets in order to avoid contamination of clean hands. **Proper handwashing process from IL Food Code Section 750.510 was provided**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - A) Plastic ice scoop had cracks in it up by the handle. Replace the ice scoop. B) Sticky, soiled foam mesh was observed under clean coffee mugs. Remove foam mesh and do not use it to line shelves. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Bottom shelf at bar holding beer buckets was damaged (chipping paint/exposed rough wood). Repair/repaint the shelf. B) Sticky, soiled foam mesh was observed lining condiment storage shelf by ice machine. Remove foam mesh, and do not use it to line any shelves. Maintain shelves clean. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) soda guns/holders (mold & fruit flies); B) (R) ice scoop holder (see #10); C) tongs hanging above fryer; D) stem thermometers; E) (R) ice machine drip guard (mold); F) pans in top holding section of prep cooler (food splash/debris in cheese slice containers); & G) clean dish drain board at bar 3 part sink (general buildup). Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) bottom inside keg cooler (mold/puddling condensation); B) (R) fryers; C) metal tables by ice machine; D) counter under silverware storage; E) bottom inside reach-in freezer; F) black crate used for storage in kitchen; & G) pan w/bags of pretzel salt and register tape in kitchen. Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Coffee mug storage area was lined with sticky, soiled foam mesh (see #14), and black cart used for storage of clean plates and bowls was soiled with crumbs. Maintain storage areas for cleaned/sanitized equipment in a manner that will protect items from potential contamination. Do not use foam mesh to line shelves. Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - A) Boxes of single service items were observed on the floor in office/dry storage area (plastic spoons & forks) and in storage area two doors down (cups, coffee filters, etc.). All boxes and storage containers must be elevated up off the floor at least 6 inches. B) Toothpicks at bar were observed intermixed with test strip bottles and other items. Store single service items in a manner that will protect them from potential contamination. Do not store toothpicks in direct contact with unclean surfaces. Single-service articles shall be stored, handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 & 1100 - A) Keg cooler waste pan drain hose empties into a plastic jug. Bottom inside of keg cooler is full of puddling liquid and buildup. Drain hose needs to be plumbed so it drains to a proper floor drain. B) Condensation was dripping from the condenser in the walkin cooler. A gray tub was being used to catch condensate, but some condensate was dripping down the wall and getting on food products (see #8). Employee noted he thought the drain line was clogged and a call for service may have already been made. Get the walkin serviced so condensation issue can be addressed. C) Drain hoses for soda guns at bar had to be removed/discarded due to presence of fruit fly life stages inside (see #35a). Manager made a call to Coke to get new drain hoses. Plumbing shall be installed, sized, and maintained in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Kitchen handsink was soiled in the basin with grimy buildup. Clean handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Dozens of fruit flies were observed in multiple areas (restrooms, dish machine room, prep area, & bar) with the most being present around soiled wiping cloths from previous evening in a pickle bucket below bread storage shelf and in soda gun holders/drain hoses. Adults and pupa (life stage between maggot & adult) were observed inside soda gun drain hoses at the bar. Hoses were removed/discarded, and Manager contacted Coke to request new hoses for soda gun holders. Areas where fruit flies have been observed need to be thoroughly cleaned, and floor drains should also be cleaned. Soiled wiping cloths need to be stored appropriately, and areas of disrepair around bread storage shelf need to be sealed (see #37). If cleaning and general maintenance alone do not alleviate the issue then contact pest control operator for service.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Floor tiles were damaged behind fryer/grill and tiles were starting to buckle under fryers. Floor along the wall, behind, and under cooking equipment was soiled. Clean the floor in the aforementioned area and replace damaged tiles. B) Recessed floor drain by kitchen handsink was soiled with moldy buildup and did not have a proper grated cover down inside. Thoroughly clean the floor drain and provide a proper cover for down inside the drain.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - Nudo board/wall where second three part sink has been removed was soiled and various gaps/holes were observed. Clean the wall and seal all holes, gaps, and crevices in the area (including juncture underneath where the bar and Nudo board meet).

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment: 750.1380b - Soiled wiping cloths were observed in a pickle bucket below the bread storage shelf, at the bar in a red sani-bucket, and on the back ledge of the beer cooler. Fruit flies were observed around soiled cloths near bread storage and in red sani-bucket. Wiping cloths were put in a garbage sack and placed in chemical closet until owner could remove from facility to be laundered. Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.
